SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
S.3, Special Branch. XXXXXX
REPORT
Date Sept. 18, 19 37.
Subject Anonymous letter addressed to subscribers of the "Shanghai Times."
Made XX and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan.

Reference the remarks of Acting Commissioner of Police,
on margin of report on above, dated 11.9.37, continued enquiries
conducted by D.S.I. Logan, D.S.I. Kao Yen Keng (S. 1) and C.D.C.
230 (S. 5) have up to date failed to elicit any information that
would assist in establishing the identity of the person or
persons responsible for distributing the anonymous letter which
forms the subject of this report.

Mr. Nottingham, proprietor of the "Shanghai Times",
when interviewed by the undersigned, stated that he had learned
that 24 distributors of the "Shanghai Times" had received copies
of the anonymous letter in question, with the words "Warning.
Stop sale at once, otherwise you will be dealt with by explosives."
added thereon in handwriting (Chinese).

（印：RECEIVED M 19 SEP. 1937 C.A.）

Only 2 of these shops are located in the Settlement,
the others being located in the French Concession.

A visit was paid to Lane 546, House 47, Tatung Road,
where the Liang Hwa (良华) Printing Works, which undertakes
the printing of the Sin Pao, is located. Nothing in the nature
of paper, envelopes, or address slips similar to those used in
the anonymous letters was found.

Mr. Nottingham stated that he was reporting the
matter to the French Police, but enquiries ascertained that the
French Police have also been unsuccessful in eliciting any
useful information in connection with the matter.

d.b.
19/9

（印：20 SEP. 1937）

Dile
D.S.I.
20/9

D. C. (Crime & Special Branches).

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 ____
S.3，特别科。XXXXXX
报告
日期：1937年9月18日。
事由：致《字林西报》（Shanghai Times）订户的匿名信。
由 D.S.I. Logan 制作并转呈。

参照代理警务总监在1937年9月11日关于上述报告的页边批注，经 D.S.I. Logan、D.S.I. 高延庚（S. 1）及 C.D.C. 230（S. 5）进行的持续调查，迄今未能获取任何有助于确定分发本报告所述匿名信之责任人身份的信息。

《字林西报》业主诺丁汉先生（Mr. Nottingham）在接受本人问询时表示，他获悉该报的24名分销商收到了上述匿名信的副本，信上手写添加了中文文字：“警告。立即停止销售，否则将用炸药对付你们。”

（印章：1937年9月19日 M 收讫 C.A.）

这些店铺中仅有2家位于租界内，其余均位于法租界。

调查人员走访了大同路546弄47号，良华印刷厂所在地，该厂承印《申报》。现场未发现与匿名信中所使用的纸张、信封或地址标签类似的物品。

诺丁汉先生表示，他正将此案报告给法国巡捕房，但经查询得知，法国巡捕房在此事上也未能获取任何有用信息。

d.b.
9月19日

（印章：1937年9月20日）

Dile
副督察长
9月20日

犯罪科及特别科科长。

S. I. Special Branch, **〔此处转录不清〕**
REPORT
Date September 11, 1937.

Subject Anonymous letter addressed to subscribers of the
"Shanghai Times"
Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

A letter containing a printed handbill in Chinese
accusing the Shanghai Times of being a propaganda paper of
the Japanese and denouncing its Chinese readers as traitors
was delivered through the post on the afternoon of Sepetember
10, to the house of the undersigned, Lane 24, No.3 Ferry
Road. The handbill together with a translation, as well
as the envelope is attached.

According to the postal mark on the envelope, it was
posted at the 23rd. Branch of the Post Office, 185 Yu Yuen
Road at 1 p.m. September 10, 1937.

The composition of this handbill as well as the type
of printing is fairly good, usually adopted in Chinese
newspaper and periodicals. The quality of the paper is
also fine and according to paper dealers paper of this kind
is of foreign make, not Japanese, and generally known as
"Dao Ling No. 20". It is extensively used by publishers
for foreign newspapers and periodicals.

The envelope of this letter is of cheap kind, commonly
used by Chinese shopkeepers for advertising purposes.

（左侧批注：）
Acc D
Source appears
likely to be
Sin Pao group.
Continue enquiries

报告
日期：1937年9月11日。

事由：致《字林西报》订户的匿名信
由首席侦探员施子良（Sih Tse-liang）制作，由 **〔此处转录不清〕** 转呈

一封内含中文印刷传单的信件，指控《字林西报》为日本人的宣传报纸，并谴责其中文读者为汉奸，于9月10日下午通过邮政投递至本人寓所，地址为斐伦路3号24弄。该传单及其译文以及信封均附后。

根据信封上的邮戳，该信于1937年9月10日下午1时在愚园路185号邮局第23支局投寄。

该传单的排版及印刷质量相当好，通常见于中文报刊杂志。纸张质量亦佳，据纸商称，此类纸张为外国制造，非日本产，通称为“道林20号”。出版商广泛将其用于外文报刊杂志。

此信的信封属于廉价种类，中国店主常用作广告宣传。

（左侧批注：）
Acc D
来源似乎
可能来自
《申报》集团。
继续调查

（左侧印章：）

上海

施子良
首席侦探员

pages.en:
TRANSLATION OF A HANDBILL DELIEVERED BY POST ON
SEPTEMBER 10. 1937 AT LANE 24. No. 3,
FERRY ROAD

" Any one who continued to purchase or read the
Shanghai Times is a traitor. The Chinese Chamber of
Commerce is expected to advise all sale agents to dis-
continue the sale.

All newspaper vendors are expected to refuse
to deliver or sell the paper.

Over 70% or 80% of the capital of the Shanghai
Times is subscribed by the Japanese. The reporters of
the Shanghai Times have long been under the wing of the
Japanese; so they do nothing but fabricate rumours in
order to mislead the world. They are our public enemy.
The Shanghai Times which disdains disgrace and misinter-
prets facts, is known as the loafer of the world press
circle.

The Shanghai Times is the propaganda paper of
our enemy in attacking China. Should any Chinese con-
tinue to sell them, he is a 100% traitor. Anyone who
continues to read it is a bona-fide traitor.

Now, look at the advertisement boards erected
by the Shanghai Times in front of Chinese shops. Is
it not stated clearly thereon, "the Japanese army has
occupied so and so"? or "so and so Chinese army has
retreated". Try to think whether there is any truth
in it. Are we all pigs?

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Cigarette
Exchange Shop Owners' Association should examine their
conscience and refuse to sell it in any shops. Every
individual should oppose our enemy and endeavour to
check the circulation of the Shanghai Times, the propaganda
paper of the Japanese".
pages.zh:
1937年9月10日投递至斐伦路3号24弄的传单译文

“凡继续购买或阅读《字林西报》者，皆为汉奸。期望上海总商会劝告所有代销商停止销售。

所有报贩应拒绝投递或销售该报。

《字林西报》超过70%或80%的资本由日本人认购。《字林西报》的记者长期受日本人庇护；因此他们除了编造谣言以误导世人外，无所事事。他们是我们的公敌。《字林西报》不顾廉耻，歪曲事实，被称为世界新闻界的无赖。

《字林西报》是敌人攻击中国的宣传报纸。若有中国人继续销售该报，他是百分之百的汉奸。任何继续阅读该报的人，是名副其实的汉奸。

现在，看看《字林西报》在中国商店前设立的广告牌。上面难道没有清楚地写着‘日军已占领某地’吗？或者‘某地中国军队已撤退’。试着想想其中是否有真实性。难道我们都是猪吗？

上海总商会和卷烟零售店同业公会应扪心自问，拒绝在任何店铺销售该报。每个人都应反对我们的敌人，并努力遏制《字林西报》这一日本宣传报纸的流通。”
